scope: Full LLVM native LDS/LES/LSS/LFS/LGS word/dword intrinsics in protected code16 with the 32-bit stack/pointer ABI. code32, x64/NeverC and the adjacent protected division path are regressions. No NeverC i386 frontend is enabled.
source_basis: Recorded base commits plus retained LLVM/NeverC patches and source-snapshot identify changed/shared inputs. Source and frozen compiler hashes were checked after the final runs. Later documentation does not affect executable inputs.

neverc_integration.reason: Upstream commits add diagnostic history while preserving the existing dev source tree. The merge changes history only; all qualified source files and compiler inputs remain identical.

count_definition: Actual executions across optimization profiles and recorded cores, not unique inputs. Protected pairs compare GPRs, flags, caches/system registers, active events and RAM against independent original bytes. Return checks are a subset that preserves compiler ABI segment invariants. x64 stopped observations are a subset of its state observations and are not added twice.
negative_controls: All six protected profiles reject a zeroed pointer loaded before an intact far-load instruction at the declared-input transport boundary.
fault_observation: Original handlers execute OUT to expose #GP/#NP/#SS/#PF, then stop immediately after completed I/O. Both original restart PCs are authenticated before normalizing the frame PC. Only inactive exception payloads are excluded after proving neither pending nor injected; all other event fields remain compared.

diagnostics.io_completion: KVM_EXIT_IO occurs before OUT completes; the runner reenters KVM and stops after OUT before observing or replacing state.
diagnostics.inactive_exception: Observed byte differences: exception.nr 14/0 and has_error_code 1/0 while injected=pending=0 on both vCPUs. The KVM implementation copies stale payloads unconditionally. Reject active exceptions, exclude only the inactive exception payload, retain all other event comparisons.
diagnostics.driver_correction: The initial x64 invocation used the newer protected-oracle CLI. It failed argument parsing without running a test. x64-retry supplies the existing --llc/--clang/--output-dir interface; the original failed log is retained and is not counted as a pass.

boundaries: Protected native coverage is CPL0 on the recorded Intel P/E cores, with a 32-bit stack/pointer ABI. It covers used/unused results, word/dword offsets, GDT null/RPL/DPL/type/present choices, nonflat/word caches, pointer alignment/cross-page/read-only cases, descriptor reads and #GP/#NP/#SS/#PF.

This does not qualify real/VM86, CPL3 #AC, asynchronous events, MOV-SS inhibition, arbitrary source-segment/address-size provenance, descriptor write faults or other CPUs. x87/SIMD state is not used by these wrappers and is outside the comparison.
Nonflat/null/read-only DS and word/nonflat SS cases stop at the native boundary. Their success does not authorize returning through a compiler frame whose segment invariants were changed.
The existing x64/NeverC oracle retains its own user-mode boundary and exclusions; it is not a complete protected-state continuation.

Production SDK neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6 and gitlink 03270359c2ed8f6806533d3832a947bf883a6f69 are unchanged. General i386 dispatch, remaining scalar/state families, real/VM86/tasks/debug, software SMM/SGX and complete CET/FRED events remain open; final SDK release/pin waits for global completion.
